members.name: Laleh
members.story: After my mother passed, I stopped speaking for almost three weeks. On the eighteenth day, a small tabby walked in through the open kitchen window, sat on my chest as I lay on the floor, and simply stayed. She did not ask me to talk. She asked me to breathe. I do not know if that is prayer. I only know it worked.

members.name: Daniel
members.story: I was not a dog person — I said so many times. Then one wet evening a yellow dog with one wonky ear followed me home from the bakery. I told him he could not stay. He stayed anyway. Within a month the panic attacks I had had for years became quieter. I do not think Badem healed me. I think Badem simply believed I was already well, and slowly I started to believe him.

members.name: Sara
members.story: Pepper came home with me on the worst winter of my life. I was cold in a way that had nothing to do with weather. She would find me wherever I sat and press her small warm forehead against my wrist — every single night, without fail, for two years. I am warm again now. I owe at least half of that to a four-kilogram black cat who never read a single book about healing.
